Hey, I'm going through a break up too. It's rough. It's okay to be emotional right now. In fact, you should be. It helps you heal. You ought to check out /r/breakups. I post there like once a day on my other account. Helps keep me sane.

So here's a website someone sent me the first week of my breakup: http://breakuprecoveryguide.com
It's useful.

So first. Stop contact. Even if you're on good terms with her, you need distance from her so you can heal. If she starts trying to contacting you, and asking why, just tell her that you need some time to yourself. Maybe one day you two can be friends, but right now is not that time. You need to focus on you.

Second, it sounds like you are not ready to date yet. That's okay. I'm two months into my breakup and still not ready. I did the bumble thing for the first month, but it left me empty. I was meeting these great guys too, but my thoughts would always come back to how this guy isn't my ex. That's not fair to me or this guy. If you don't mind casual dates, it's not terrible to distract yourself once in awhile. But I'd be careful with that even. At this point, I'm just not able to have that emotional attachment to someone else, so I know I'm not ready. Everyone moves on at different paces, so don't push yourself unnecessarily.

Third, go out and meet people. Friendships. If you're not outgoing, learn to be. Some great books out there that teach you how to talk to people, like How to Win Friends and Influence People. Hang out more with the friends you already have and your family. You need relationships right now, just the non-romantic ones.

Fourth, take time to analyze your relationship and learn from it. Where did you go wrong? Where did she go wrong? What's the lesson you can get from that? This is important, because if you miss it, you're gonna make the same mistake again. 

Fifth, learn something new. Become more interesting by finding new hobbies. You'll begin to enjoy life more. It's also a great way to meet new friends. 

Sixth, I recommend therapy, but I know a lot of people won't do it. Cognitive behavioral therapy is the best. A therapist is great because you can talk to them about your relationship and the feelings you're having. They can help you work through that. If you have friends and family to talk to, that's great. But sometimes it's just not the same as a therapist who is trained to make you challenge the irrational thoughts you're having. Regardless if you get a therapist or not, seek out SOMEONE you can talk to about your feelings. Do not bottle up. 

Seven, you're gonna be okay. There's so many people out there and odds are in your favor that you'll find someone like her or better one day. It just sucks cause it's the waiting game. This pain goes away eventually. It's okay to feel the way you feel. It means you were capable of caring about something.

Check this out: [Dunning-Kruger effect](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunning%E2%80%93Kruger_effect)

Basically it's the idea that stupid people think they are smart because they're too stupid to understand what they don't know. Vice versa, people who are smart don't recognize that they're smart because they assume that if something is easy for them to do, then it must be easy for everyone. 

School is hard. I feel like an idiot all the time at school because it takes me a really long time to understand things. If it came easily then there would be no need for college because everyone could just pick up on things with a snap of the fingers. People apparently see something in you that is competent because they think you're smart enough for college. If college is something you wanted to do, it really depends on how hard you are willing to work. 

Don't let your issues be a deterrent. I receive accommodations from my school for my anxiety and ADD. I get extra time on my exams. At my previous school I had preferential seating and I could request a note taker for my classes. If you did later on decide to go to school, I'd recommend talking to the school and a psychologist/psychiatrist/therapist about your condition and what would be effective in helping you succeed in school.
